A generator that gives one row per combination of world elements

Source: R/synthetic_grid.R
synthetic_grid_generator.Rd

Returns a function(profile, n, seed, world) for the generator of a synthetic spec. The function gives one row for each combination of the world elements in grid, and draws the other columns with csdb::simulate_from_profile().

Usage

synthetic_grid_generator(grid, finish = NULL)

Arguments

grid

A character vector of names of world elements.

finish

NULL, or a function(d, seed, world) that returns the data.table d with values for one table.

Value

A function(profile, n, seed, world) that returns a data.table.

Details

The generator works in this order:

  1. It stops when world is NULL or does not hold every element of grid.

  2. It takes one unit from each element of grid. A vector is one column of unique values. A data.frame gives its columns that are in names(profile$field_types), as unique rows, so the values in one row stay together. An element with no column in the table is skipped.

  3. It crosses the units. data.table::CJ() crosses the vectors, in the order of grid, and each data.frame is then crossed with every row so far. The grid is the result.

  4. It calls csdb::simulate_from_profile() for nrow(grid) rows, with seed. It removes profile$keys, because the grid makes the rows unique. It removes every data.frame element from the world. csdb draws wrong values for a data.frame element named like a TEXT column, and stops for one named like an INTEGER column.

  5. It replaces each grid column of the draw with the grid.

  6. It calls finish(d, seed, world) when finish is not NULL. world is the world as the generator got it, with its data.frame elements.

  7. It orders the columns as names(profile$field_types), and returns the data.table.

The generator ignores n: the grid sets the number of rows. For a partitioned table, put the partition column in the world and in grid, so that every partition gets every combination.

The generator stops when the elements of grid give no column of the table, or give one column twice. It installs the grid values with their R types, so a world element MUST have the R type of its column. synthetic_weeks() and synthetic_years() give the time columns with those types.

Examples

generator <- synthetic_grid_generator(c("location", "age", "weeks"))
world <- list(
  location = data.frame(
    location_code = c("nation_nor", "county_nor03"),
    granularity_geo = c("nation", "county")
  ),
  age = c("total", "000_004"),
  weeks = synthetic_weeks("2024-01", "2024-03")
)
profile <- csdb::profile_schema(
  c(location_code = "TEXT", granularity_geo = "TEXT", age = "TEXT",
    isoyearweek = "TEXT", n = "INTEGER"),
  keys = c("location_code", "age", "isoyearweek")
)
generator(profile, n = NULL, seed = 1L, world = world)
#>     location_code granularity_geo     age isoyearweek     n
#>            <char>          <char>  <char>      <char> <int>
#>  1:    nation_nor          nation   total     2024-01    38
#>  2:    nation_nor          nation   total     2024-02    50
#>  3:    nation_nor          nation   total     2024-03    41
#>  4:  county_nor03          county   total     2024-01     5
#>  5:  county_nor03          county   total     2024-02    23
#>  6:  county_nor03          county   total     2024-03    31
#>  7:    nation_nor          nation 000_004     2024-01    13
#>  8:    nation_nor          nation 000_004     2024-02     1
#>  9:    nation_nor          nation 000_004     2024-03    44
#> 10:  county_nor03          county 000_004     2024-01    17
#> 11:  county_nor03          county 000_004     2024-02    21
#> 12:  county_nor03          county 000_004     2024-03    77
